anya: heads-up, HF->Redwood conversion on `llama-like-v2` produced a weird tokenizer split. We have a `tokenizer.json` (fast) in the HF artifact but `tokenizer_config.json` in the same repo references the slow tokenizer class and there's no `special_tokens_map.json`. After conversion Redwood runtime silently fell back to the slow tokenizer and our evals show a clear quality delta after quantization :bug:
sam: ugh. can you paste the file list from the model dir? is `vocab.json` + `merges.txt` present or only `tokenizer.json`?
anya: listing: `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `config.json`, `pytorch_model.bin` (weights), no `vocab.json`, no `merges.txt`, no `special_tokens_map.json`. Looks like the HF model originally used a fast/tokenizers-built tokenizer; someone regenerated a config that points at `PreTrainedTokenizer` (slow) without adding the old files.
mike: that explains fallback. Redwood loader prefers `tokenizer.json` fast path but if `tokenizer_config.json` explicitly sets `tokenizer_class` to a slow class we currently fall back to the slow path to preserve semantics. If supporting files are missing slow path still loads but defaults specials differently.
anya: error snippet from our eval job:```
WARNING:root:Using slow tokenizer; missing fast files.
Tokenization mismatch: expected 1.8% OOV vs baseline 0.2%
Eval (lm-ppl): quantized run PPL 9.6 -> baseline 6.3 (delta +3.3)
```
zara: repro steps for fix: either (A) regenerate `tokenizer.json` from HF `AutoTokenizer` and push, or (B) edit `tokenizer_config.json` to remove the slow `tokenizer_class` override and add `special_tokens_map.json`. Which is faster?
anya: fastest is (A) for this model. I can run `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('./model'); t.save_pretrained('./model')"` locally and upload.
sam: also add a smoke test in conversion script to assert consistency: if `tokenizer_config.json` references a slow class but `tokenizer.json` exists, warn and prefer fast unless explicit override present. Put a one-line lint: compare token counts for a probe set.
mike: short-term runtime mitigation (if we can't push new artifact immediately): add a translation map at Redwood serving layer that maps missing special tokens to the slow-tokenizer equivalents and remaps token ids for prompt templates. I can sketch that mapping.
anya: sketch pls — the immediate eval regression is from chat templates tokenization: opening system prompt gets tokenized 8 tokens longer with slow tokenizer which changes KV caching and chunk boundaries; that triggers different generation edges in quantized kernels.
mike: sketch:```
# runtime mapping (pseudo)
map_specials = {
  "<|endoftext|>": "</s>",
  "<|pad|>": "<pad>",
}
# apply after tokenization fallback: for token in toks: if tok in map_specials_rev: replace
```
zara: sounds good. I'll take the conversion/lint change in the `hf-to-redwood` toolchain once anya uploads regenerated files.
eval-bot: automated eval report attached: baseline (non-quant) rouge-L: 0.412, quant (with slow tokenizer fallback): 0.374, delta -0.038. run id: r-2026-03-19-42
anya: plan: 1) regenerate `tokenizer.json` and `special_tokens_map.json` and push to model bucket (eta 2h). 2) sam to add lint/warn in conversion script (eta EOD). 3) mike to prepare runtime mapping PR as emergency guard (eta 24h). 4) zara to rerun stage evals after push and report numbers. I'll update this thread when done. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — also add unit that tokenizes 1000 random prompts and computes tokenization divergence %, fail conversion if >0.5% by default (opt-out flag for exotic cases).
mike: noted, will start prototype for mapping.
anya: updating now, will ping when push complete :eyes:
